questions.answer: Functional class with 6-minute walk distance, and NT-proBNP

In pulmonary hypertension, when are large haemodynamic swings most likely?
questions.answer: At induction and with positive pressure ventilation

questions.stem: Why avoid acute rises in PVR during pulmonary hypertension anaesthesia?
questions.answer: They raise RV afterload and cut RV output

questions.stem: In pulmonary hypertension anaesthesia, why keep mean arterial pressure up?

questions.answer: Maintain RV contractility and optimise RV preload

questions.answer: Guiding vasopressors and an index of RV preload

questions.stem: Why give vasoconstrictors alongside anaesthesia in pulmonary hypertension?
questions.answer: To hold SVR and MAP for RV perfusion

questions.stem: When should a pulmonary hypertension patient be extubated after surgery?
questions.answer: Only when awake, fully reversed and ventilating well
